ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Import of pepper 
*301.SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: Will the Minister of 
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government allowed pepper import from other countries and if 
so, how many nations have been allowed free trade of pepper with our country; 
(b) whether the pepper of Vietnam has been routed to India through Sri 
Lanka by misusing free trade import facilities and if so, whether Government 
initiated any steps to check the misuse of trading provisions; and 
(c) whether Government propose to set up any limitation for the import 
policy to check the misuse of the concerned provisions? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. India imports pepper from countries like Vietnam, Sri Lanka, 
Indonesia, Ecuador, Singapore, Thailand, Brazil, Netherlands, Malaysia and 
Madagascar etc. However, duty free import of pepperisonly allowed from Sri 
Lanka under India-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreement (ISLFTA). 
(b) The Government is not aware of any routing of Vietnamese Pepper to 
India through Sri Lanka under ISLFTA. All exports of pepper from Sri Lanka 
to India are accompanied by a Certificate of Origin issued by the Department 
of Commerce, Government of Sri Lanka. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2005] 
(c) The Foreign Trade Policy permits import of pepper in the following ways: 
(i) Import of pepper under Chapter-9 of the ITC (HS) Classification of 
Imports and Exports is free subject to payment of Customs Duty. 
(ii) Export Oriented Units (EOUs) and Special Economic Zones (SEZs) 
are allowed duty free import for value addition and reexport purpose. 
(iii) Import against Advance License is also allowed for value addition and 
re-export purpose. However, Advance Licenses for pepper are issued 
only for import of "Light Black Pepper" for extraction by oleoresin 
industry for export purposes. 
(iv) Import is also allowed under the Free Trade Agreement with Sri Lanka 
at Zero Duty irrespective of end use. 
(v) Under the Plant Quarantine Order, an import permit is required for 
import of pepper. 
Action taken by Government: 
(a) Advance Licence are issued only for import of "light black pepper" for 
extraction by oleoresin industry for export purpose. (Public Notice 
No. 17 dated 7.6.2005). 
(b) DTA sales by EOUs at concessional duty and at full duty has been 
disallowed in case of pepper and pepper products. (Notification No. 
2 dated 13.5.2005). 
(c) It is now mandatory for EOU units to get themselves registered with 
the Spices Board (PN 21 dated 13.6.2005). 
(d) Import of 300 sensitive items including spices are monitored by the 
DGFT so that Government can take  action in case of any surge in 
imports.

(a) and (b) The names of Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) which 
have been blacklisted by the Council for Advancement of People's Action and 
Rural Technology (CAPART) due to their involvement in corrupt practices and/or

documents/information in support of their credentials.

independent empanelled monitors.

objectivity in the selection of facilitator-cum-Evalutiors.

are made mandatory in order to avoid funding to the NGOs run be prosy/non-
existent NGOs etc.

passbook and registration certificates, before the release funds, to avoid funding 
to the NGOs to check forgery and fabrication of doucments.

CAPART as their credibility is much better than be individual Monitors.

martial where—

justice and discipline for all the three forces

2289. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that United Nations' Conference on Trade 
Development has asked India to accelerate the development of its 
manufacturing industry instead of concentrating on IT based services, to 
maintain its GDP growth; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) what is the action plan of Government to ensure further productivity gains 
in manufacturing sector? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN): (a) The Trade and 
Development Report (TDR) 2005 published by United Nations' Conference 
on Trade Development (UNCTAD) echoes the sentiment 
83 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2005] 
that in India, the share of industry in GDP has remained constant while that of 
services has risen rapidly. This might pose a challenge for sustained growth, as 
productivity increases in the services sector are normally less strong than in the 
manufacturing sector. Therefore, it would be important to acelerate the 
development of its manufacturing industry for India to be able to maintain its 
GDP growth. 
(b) The TDR points out that a shift towards manufacturing is crucial in India, 
if it is to sustain its impressive economic performance. Though TDR does not 
clearly suggest a focus on manufacturing sector at the expense of the IT based 
services sector, it expresses uncertainty whether their share in India's export 
earnings can rise much further-thereby making a case for the Indian IT sector to 
move up the value addition chain and not remain trapped at the low end'of the 
market, exporting services such as debugging, testing, conversion and 
installation of software. The TDR observed that historically, there has been no 
case of economic catch-up based on the development of the services sector 
where the scope for productivity gains is more limited than in manufacturing. 
While the IT revolution has certainly changed the potential for the services 
sector to support rapid growth in develo ping countries, the size of the world 
market for IT based services is smal ler than that for manufactures. The TDR 
also strongly advocates, for both China and India, technology up-gradation to 
support more diversified and higher value added production to maintain economic 
growth, as more developing countries develop capacities to produce labour-
intensive manufactured goods resulting in higher competition in manufactured 
exports. It also indicates that in India export dynamism in manufacturing is 
likely to become stronger and that it is widely expected that improvement in 
transport facilities and continued reforms with improvement in transport could 
reduce current disadvantage of other sectors (other than IT) in exporting. 
(c) The Government has put in place various policies to promote industrial 
growth. Besides delicensing of industrial capacity, liberalisation of foreign trade 
regime to provide better access to inputs at competitive prices and 
rationalization and reduction of customs and excise were carried forward. 
The Budget 2005-2006 also contains a number of measures related to 
manufacturing and infrastructure, envisaging favourable impact on industrial 
growth. Besides, Industrial Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme (IIUS) has been 
launched to enhance international

competitiveness of the domestic industr y by providing quality infrastructure 
in functional clusters. The National Manufacturing Competitiveness Council 
(NMCC) has been set up by the Government to provide a continuing forum for 
policy dialogue to energise and sustain the growth of manufacturing industries 
in India.

manufacturing practices followed by some factories. Good quality leaf continues

formula between the small tea growers an d manufacturers of tea with effect

share of the price obtained by the manufacturer for made tea and implementation 
of a Special Tea Term Loan (STTL) which inter alia provides for sanctioning 
of working capital limits up to Rs. 2 lakhs at a concessional rate of interest not

245. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA:  Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the extent of damage to the crops-human life, cattle, habitation and 
highways due to floods in the various part s of the country in last three years, 
up to date; 
(b) the details in terms of value of the damaged crops and the area affected, 
human lives lost, cattle drowned, houses collapsed and highways damaged, State-
wise and year-wise; 
(c) the steps taken/contemplated to be taken, to find a permanent solution 
to endemic floods; 
(d) whether Government have a mechanism to monitor the actual disbursal of help 
to the affected persons, so that the scam is not repeated; and 
(e) if so, details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) and (d) Details showing the year-wise damage to 
crops, human lives, catties and habitation during the last three year i.e. 2002-03, 
2003-04 and 2004-05 are given in the statement (See below). The estimated 
everage value of damage to crops and houses du to heavy rains and floods in the 
last three years i.e. from 2002 to 2004 comes to approximately Rs. 984.329 
crore and Rs. 751.739 crore respectively. 
(c) Flood cannot be fully controlled. It is managed from place to place on the 
technical merits of the problem. However, flood Management being within the 
purview of the States, the schemes for flood control are planned, funded and 
executed by the State Governments. Th e role of Central Government is 
technical, catalytic and promotional in nature. 
Central Government has been initiating various measures for assisting the 
States in the management of flood. The Rashtriya Barh Ayog and several 
other Expert Committees have been constituted by the Government from time 
to time to study the problem relating to floods and its management, the 
recommendations of which were sent to the respective State Governments for 
implementation. Ganga Flood Control Commission for Ganga Basin States 
prepared comprehensive Plans on Flood Management for all the 23 river 
systems of Ganga. Likewise, 
128 

[14 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Brahmaputra Board prepared Master Plans for Flood Management for the 
Brahmaputra, Barak and its major tributaries. These plans were forwarded to 
concerned State Governments for implementation. 
In order to mitigate the damage from floods, a nationwide flood 
forecasting and warning system, as a non-structural measure, has been 
established by the Central Water Commi ssion, which issues flood forecasts 
at 173 stations. 
As a long-term measure for flood management, agreement has been reached 
with Nepal for survey and investigation and preparation of detailed Project Reports 
for Sapta Kosi High Dam Multipurpose Project and Sun Kosi Storage Cum 
Diversion Scheme for which a Joint Project Office has already been opened in 
Nepal in August 2004. This Project envisages flood control as one of the major 
benefits. The Government of India has also been providing Central assistance to 
the Sate Governments to take up critical anti erosion/flood management 
works. 
(d) and (e) As per the existing Scheme for financing relief expenditure, the 
State Governments are primarily responsible for undertaking relief and 
rehabilitation measures in the areas a ffected by natural calamities and for 
distribution of relief on ground. The Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the State Governments by providing financial and logistic support, 
where necessary. 
As per the Relief Schemes of Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) and National 
Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF), th e expenditure is to be incurred 
according to the approved items and norms  of expenditure. The Ministry of 
Home Affairs has prescribed a performa for submission of information by the 
State Governments on expenditure from CRF/NCCF, on a monthly basis. The 
Ministry of Home Affairs have also  requested the State Governments to 
maintain proper record of relief operations and distribution with a view to have 
transparency in Relief Operations. 
The States Accountant Generals have also been requested to monitor the 
expenditure as per the items and norms of assistance. The Schemes inter alia 
provide that the Comptroller and Auditor General of India would cause audit of 
CRF every year in terms of the purpose of the CRF Scheme. The State 
Government shall furnish a copy of the audit report of the Comptroller and 
Auditor General of India in respect of CRF to the Ministry of Finance and to the 
Ministry-of Home Affairs.

2348. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the increasing incidents of crimes 
against women are having bad impact on the visiting tourists of the capital; 
and 
(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) and (b) A total of 11,18,663 foreign tourists have 
visited Delhi upto 30th November of the current year as  against 10,73,418 
during the entire year of 2004. 
However, the Government has taken a number of steps to prevent crime 
against women including establishment of Crime Against Women 
133 

RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2005] 
Cells; setting up of Rape Crises Intervention Centres in all the nine Police 
Districts; association of Women Police Officers and NGO in investigation of rape 
cases; setting up of three Special Courts headed by women judges; networking with 
Non-Governmental Organisations; deployment of staff in plain clothes at 
vulnerable places; starting of dedicated telephone help lines; and constitution of 
'Women Mobile Team' to attend to distress calls from women on round-the-
clock basis; providing counselling through the NGOs to the needy complainant; 
seeking help of NGOs and professionals such as social workers, doctors, 
psychologists, lawyers and special counsellors during the investigation of rape 
cases; association of NGOs to assist the  victims during medical examination 
and for counselling, treatment, reha bilitation, Self-Defence training 
programme and the recently launched scheme "Parivartan" under which lady 
beat constables have been deployed in selected slum areas. 
The Government has also taken a number of steps to prevent crime against 
foreign and domestic tourists which include keeping surveillance over the areas 
frequented by tourists including taxi/auto's leaving airports along with tourists; 
running of Pre-paid Fare Booths; issue of complaint cards to passengers 
availing taxi facility at the airports; launching of a drive to verify the character 
and antecedents of taxi drivers operating at Indira Gandhi International Airport 
and issue of Public Service Vehicle Badges to them; and taking of stringent 
steps to eliminate the menance of tours at the airports. In addition, keeping in 
view the importance of Delhi as a tourist destination, Delhi Police has 
launched a scheme on 6.8.2004 to help tourists including foreign tourists to 
overcome the problems of transport, accommodation, tourism-related

Rice subsidy for Sri Lankan refugees 
2351. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had withdrawn the rice subsidy 
scheme for Sri Lankan Tamil refugees; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that Government of Tamil Nadu had demanded 
restoration of rice subsidy for Sri Lankan refugees; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Government of India have 
discontinued provision of subsidized ration to Sri Lankan refugees in Refugee 
Camps in Tamil Nadu vide orders issued on 5th August, 2005. 
The Government of Tamil Nadu was requested (inte-alia) in June, 2005 to 
furnish instructions (if any) for indefinite supply (beyond 3 months) of 
subsidized rice to Refugees in Refugee Camps. The Government of Tamil Nadu 
have not been able to provide instructions for indefinite supply of subsidized 
rice to Refugees in Refugee Camps. Nor has this Ministry been able to locate 
any such instructions.' 
The Ministry of Labour & Rehabilitation, Department of Rehabilitation's letter 
No.1 (7)/73-RH.I dated 10th September 1973, which is quoted by the 
Government of Tamil Nadu as the basis for claiming reimbursement for 
Refugees in Refugee Camps, was specifi cally applicable for Repatriates in 
one Transit Camps, at Mandapam. However, the same was made applicable to 
Refugees in Transit Camps by Ministry of Labour & Rehabilitation's letter 
No.1(26)/83-RH.I dated 19th December, 1983. 
Under the said letter of 1973 & 1983, subsidized ration and cash doles were 
made admissible (with conditions specified therein) for a maximum period of 3 
months only, and in only Transit Camp/s. 
The practice of (indefinitely) providing subsidized ration and cash doles to 
Refugees in Refugee Camps has been continuing (irrespective of whether or 
not specific instructions in this regard are available). 
138 

[14 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
The system of supply of subsidized ration to refugees from Food 
Corporation of India (FCI), through Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation 
(TNCSC), and subsequent reimburseme nt to the State Government, is 
administratively cumbersome. From the financial aspect, utilisation 
certificates/audit certificates for the expenditure incurred by the Government 
of Tamil Nadu on supply of (interalia) subsidized ration are unduly delayed. 
Refugees also earn and have free movement (for their livelihood) outside 
the Refugee Camps. 
The rates of cash doles (irrespective of whether or not specific instructions 
to make them applicable to Refugees in Refugee Camps or to extend them 
beyond 3 months are available or not) have been periodically revised. 
As per the Government of India's letter of 1973 the amount to be charged 
from the beneficiary was fixed at 57 paise per kilogram, and the difference upto 
the actual sale price of the cheapest vari ety fit for consumption as avaiable in 
Fair Price Shops was to be borne as subsidy by Government of India. Thus, the 
amount to be charged was fixed in absolute terms and not even as a percentage 
of the actual sale price of the cheapest variety fit for consumption. Due to this 
lacuna in the Government letter of 1973 the sale price of the cheapest variety 
fit for consumption kept on steadily increasing ove the years, thereby increasing 
the amount of subsidy every year. 
Having regard to the above, the practice of supply of subsidized ration in 
Refugee Camps, with concomitant administrative/financial problems, and with 
the inherent lacuna in the letter of 1973, was appropriate to be discontinued. 
Therefore, irrespective of the fact wh ether Government of India's orders 
for indefinite supply of subsidized ration to Sri Lankan refugees exist or not, 
provision of subsidized ration to Sri Lankan Refugees in Refugee camps was 
discontinued with immediate effect vide orders issued on 5th August 2005. 
However, Sri Lankan refugees staying in refugee camps have been allowed to 
be provided the facility to purchase rice from Fair Price Shops at the 
prescribed rates (i.e., at normal Fair Price Shop rates). 
139 

RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2005] 
. (c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in her letter dated 
23rd August 2005 had requested Government of India to restore the rice 
subsidy for the refugees in Refugee Camps. 
The matter was re-examined. It was found that there was no case for re-
constderation on the decision of discontinuing subsidized rations for refugees 
in Refugee Camps.

DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the districts in the country when National Food for Work Programme is 
being implemented in the country, State-wise; 
(b) the critetion being adopted for the implementation of the programme and the

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) The State-wise 
names of 150 most backward districts identified for the implementation of 
NFFWP is given is the statement (See below). 
(b) The National Food for Work Programme (NFFWP ) aims at 
generation of additional supplementary wage employment with food security 
through creation of socio economic infrastructure that re-generate natural resource 
base and create infrastructure having potential to provide employment on sustained 
basis in the rural areas of the identified districts. These backward district have 
been identified on the basis of an exercise undertaken by the Planning 
Commission using three parameters, namely (i) agricultural productivity per 
worker, (ii) agricultural wage rate and (iii) SC/ST population. At least one 
district had been selected in each State. All the States except Goa have been 
covered.

the NFFWP at present. The NFFWP will subsume with National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) which will be implemented in 200 
districts in first phase. The remaining districts will be covered within 5 years 
under NREGA. 
(e) and (f) There is no proposal to include areas revaged by natural 
calamities since, NREGA being an ongoing wage employment generation 
programme with defined objectives for which districts have been identified based 
on set criteria.

DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact the Union Government with UNICEF has funded the 
Information, Education and Communication (IEC) in rural sanitation 
campaign in Karnataka;

sanitation?

DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Information, 
Education & Communication (IEC) is an  integral part of Total Sanitation 
Campaign (TSC) projects, which have been sanctioned by Union Government 
in all rural districts of Karnataka. Total project outlay of TSC projects in 
Karnataka is Rs. 325.03 crore. Share of Union Government, State Government 
and Community are Rs. 207.15 crore, Rs. 73.28 crore and Rs. 44.60 crore 
respectively. Union Government has so far released Rs. 64.37 crore to these 
Projects. In addition, Union Government has supported the State 
Communication and Capacity Development Unit (CCDU) for taking up IEC 
and capacity building activities in the State for which fund of Rs. 120.59 lakh

lakh for supporting CCDU during 2005.

reward scheme, Nirmal Gram Puraskar for Panchayati Raj Institutions,

2397. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of 
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government's proposed schemes for uplifitment 
of rural India have failed to achieve the target due to inadequate mechanism of 
dissemination of information amongst the rural population; 
(b) if so, what steps Government propose or have taken to give due 
publicity of the schemes in the rural areas of the country; 
(c) the system for monitoring the progress of the implementation of such 
scheme; and 
(d) as large part of rural India is out of reach of print/electronic media, 
whether Government will involve the elected public representatives for proper 
implementation of the scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL): (a) and (b) The 
Ministry of Rural Development is implementing a number of schemes through 
State Govemments/UT Administrations for upliftment of the rural poor in the 
country. These schemes are reviewed through various monitoring mechanism 
regularly and according to the Progress Reports r eceived from the State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations, the performance of these 
schemes has been found to be satisfactory. In view of the magnitude of 
disseminating information to a vast population of rural poor and of ensuring 
participation of the society in rural development, Information, Education and 
Communication activities have been substantially scaled up through print 
media, electronic media and 
193 

RAJYA SABHA [14 December, 2005] 
out door publicity. The Ministry is also bringing out a monthly Newsletter 
'Gramin Bharat' in order to keep the Panchayti Raj Institution's informed about 
the various programmes. 
(c) The Ministry has developed a comprehensive system of Monitoring the 
implementation and impact of the progr ammes including utilization of funds 
through Periodical Progress Reports, Performance Review Committee, Area 
Officer's Scheme, Vigilance and Monitoring Committee, National Level 
Monitors, Quick Evaluation Studies, Impact Assessment Studies for improving 
the quality of work and adherence of implementation of schemes as per 
programme guidelines. Besides, the State have been advised to adopt a four-
pronged strategy consisting of (i) creation of awareness about the schemes, (ii) 
transparency (iii) People's Partnership and (iv) accountability. 
(d) The Ministry of Rural Development has assigned a central role to the 
elected representatives at all levels both in implementation and monitoring of 
the schemes.

Project under RGNDWM projects 
2399. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission have been 
launched; 
(b) if so, the details of the funds allocated to each project in different States, 
district-wise details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that there are projects pending for completion in various 
districts; 
(d) if so, details of the unfinished projects under this scheme in different States with 
particular reference to Alappuzha in Kerala; and 
(e) the reasons for the delay? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI A. NARENDRA): (a) The Technology Mission on drinking 
water management, called the National Drinking Water Mission was formed in 1986. 
This was renamed as Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water Mission (RGNDWM) in 
1991. It extends financial assistance to the States to supplement their efforts of taking 
up rural drinking water and sanitation sector schemes under the Centrally 
Sponsored Schemes, namely Accele rated Rural Water Supply Programme 
(ARWSP) and Central Rural Sanitation Programme (CRSP) respectively. Powers to plan 
sanction, implement and execute individual rural drinking water supply schemes vest with 
State Governments. The details of the drinking water projects taken up by the States 
from the funds of ARWSP and the status of those projects are not maintained at the 
Central level except in case of Sector Reform Projects, and Swajaldhara projects 
sanctioned in the year 2002-2003. Under CRSP, Total Sanitation Campaign Projects 
(TSC) have been launched since 1999. 
(b) Under various components of ARWSP, State-wise allocation is made based on a 
laid down criterion. Funds are not allocated project-wise. The State-wise allocation 
made during 2005-06 under different components of ARWSP is given in the 
Statement-I (See below). TSC projects have been sanctioned in 540 districts of the country 
so far. State- 
202 

[14 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
wise outlay of funds sanctioned and released is given in the Statement-ll. 
(c) to (e) The details of the drinking water projects taken up by the States from the 
funds of ARWSP and the status of those projects are not maintained at the Central level 
except in case of Sector Reform Projects, Swajaldhara projects sanctioned in the year 
2002-03 and TSC projects sanctioned since 1999. No projects were approved for 
Alappuzha district of Kerala under Sector Reforms Projects and Swajaldhara in the year 
2002-03. TSC project for Alappuzha district has been sanctioned in 2001 -02 with an outlay of 
Rs. 1656.13 lakhs and Central share of Rs. 1100.05 lakhs, of which Rs. 660.04 lakhs has 
been released so far. TSC projects normally take 4-5 years to complete and the project for 
Alappuzha is an ongoing project, hence there is no delay.

Exemption of Textiles from VAT purview 
2411. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that all textile items, which are now excluded from 
VAT will attract VAT from next year; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that some States are opposing to include textile 
items from VAT's purview; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the percentage of tax going to be imposed on textile items; and 
(e) what the Ministry is doing in this regard to convince the Finance 
Ministry to exempt textiles from VAT's purview? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VEGHELA): 
(a) The levy of "tax on sale or purchase of goods within a State" is a State 
subject under Entry 54 of List-ll (State List) in the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India. Accordingly an Empowered Committee of State 
Finance Ministers (EC) has been constituted to take decisions on all 
parameters relating to St ate VAT, including the rates of taxes on various 
commodities.   
(b) and (c) At present certain categories of textile fabrics, which are subject 
to Additional Excise Duty (AED), by the centre under the Additional Duties of 
Excise (Goods of Special Importance) Act, 1957, are exempt from levy of sales 
tax/VAT. The States receive a portion of the revenue of AED collected by the 
centre as per the formula recommended by the Finance Commission, in lieu of 
sales tax/VAT on such fabrics. However, AED on these items has been 
abolished with effect from August 2004. Accordingly the Empowered 
Committee of State Finance Ministers is designated to take a further decision on 
imposing VAT on such categories of textile fabrics. 
 
Further certain items like handloom fabrics, khadi garments/made-ups, 
cotton and silk yarn in hank etc. are exempt from payment of State VAT. 
(d) and (e) The Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers is 
designated to look into all aspects of levying sales tax/VAT and rates 
220 

[14 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
thereof, on all categories of textiles items. The Committee has not yet given its 
recommendations in the matter. 
Action plan for NTC mills 
† 2412.     SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA:           
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whethir it is a fact that a decision has been taken to close down the 65 mills of 
National Textile Corporation, run 30 mills in joint venture with private sector and 
modernize 22 mills; 
(b) if so, the facts in this regard; 
(c) whether Government have formulated any action plan regarding all the said 
mills; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and by when the said action plan would be implemented 
finally? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): (a) to (d) 
Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) approved revival schemes for 8 
Subsidiary Corporations in February and July, 2002 and Government of India approved a 
separate scheme for the 9th Subsidiary Corporation of NTC(TN&P) in 2002. As per these 
approved schemes 66 unviable mills were to be closed and 53 viable mills to be modernized 
and revived. The resources required for this are to be met through sale of assets of closed 
mills and surplus assets of working mills. 
Accordingly, NTC has closed down 65 unviable mills under the ID Act, transferred one 
unviable mill along with one viable mill located in Pondicherry to the State 
Government of Pondicherry. 
The Government of India has now decided to modernize 22 viable mills in the 1st 
phase by NTC through sale of surplus assets and 29 mills in 2nd phase by seeking private 
partnership through Joint Venture. Besides this, the land of one mill is proposed to 
be used for the construction of India International Trade Tower in Mumbai. 1st Phase of 
modernisation is expected to be completed in 2006-07 depending on the availability of 
funds from sale of surplus lands.

setting up their textile units, Government has launched the 'Scheme for

Rehabilitation of persons unemployed due to closure of textile 
units 
2419. SHRI T.T.V DHINAKARAN: W ill the Minister of TEXTILES be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the number of persons rendered unemployed by closure of textile units; 
(b) the number of persons rehabilitated during the past three years; and 
(c) the detaits of schemes implemented for rehabilitation of retrenched 
workers? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI. SHANKERSINH VAGHELA); 
(a) As on 31 st October, 2005 there were 3,42,048 workers on the rolls of closed 
textile mills. 
(b) During the last three years, 4621 workers have been paid relief to the 
extent of Rs. 13.21 crore. 
(c) The Government of India has formulated the Textile Workers' 
Rehabilitation Fund Scheme (TWRFS) with effect from 15th September, 1986 to 
give interim relief to the workers rendered jobless due to permanent closure of 
the textile mills. Relief under the scheme is available only for three years on a 
tapering basis-75% of the wage equivalent in the first year, 50% in the second 
year and 25% in the third year. The mills closed on or after 6.6.1985 are covered 
under the Scheme. This scheme is not applicable to the State/Central 
Government Public Sector Undertakings and the textile units in the 
cooperative fold of the State/Central Government.

Adverse effect of Chinese garments 
2421. SHRI VARINDER SINGH BAJWA: Will the Minister of TEXTILES 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Chinese garm ents sold in Indian markets have 
adversely affected the Indian Textile Industry; and 
(b) if so, how Government propose to meet the situation? 
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI SHANKERSINH VAGHELA): 
(a) and (b) Chinese garments are sold in Indian market at a competitive price as 
China has certain edge over India in respect of infrastructure, raw material 
costs, tariff structure, power-rates, etc. However, the import ot Chinese garments 
into the country has posed no considerable threat to the domestic i ndustry as 
no complaint has been received from the Indan Textile Industry in this 
regard. India's import of garments from Chira in 2004-05 has actually declined 
to Rs. 22 crore from Rs. 23 crore in 2003-04.

Concern over non-allocation of funds towards achieving

SHRI K.B. KRISHNAMURTHY (Karnataka): Sir, by inserting 
the word "socialist' in the preambl e of the Constitution, the State 
stands committed to eliminate inequalities in income, status and 
standards of life. But it has done little to translate this solemn pledge

been brought about by any Government al edict or statute. Shri 
Rammohan Roy, Periyar Ramaswamy Naicker, Mahatma Phule and 
Dr. Ambedkar had set ablaze this process, which, cumulatively, has 
jolted the dalits out of bondage which they have been suffering for 
over generations.

subjected to most inhuman and atro cious treatment by both the State 
and the society by forcing them to carry human excreta. The Centre's 
directives to enforce this pledge to States in a time-bound manner are 
still to be implemented. Though a paltry sum of Rs.30 crores was 
allocated for the Centrally sponsored low Cost Sanitation Scheme for

Dalits, especially to attain a 'Zero manual scavenging' status for the 
entire 
nation within a definite time-frame.

ally themselves or align themselves to this international standard.

fresh survey of below poverty line and above poverty line cardholders. 
Fake cards, corruption by fair price shop owners, indifference 
of bureaucracy and political leadership towards the PDS mar the 
system. Even the common people know little about the PDS. 
The vigilance committees appointed to keep check on the 
PDS are useless since they are filled with politicians. Even if the shop

punished. When these evils will be re moved, the needy section of the 
population will get benefit of the PDS.

Government should accept the recommendation made by the
